the presence of a gain at ERB2/17q or a loss at DDC/18q is associated with a decreased 4‐year survival, and the combined presence of both alterations is associated with a significantly decreased survival.

a new prognostic marker for Stage II–III colon cancer.
the identification of molecular prognostic biomarkers in Stage II–II colon cancer.
a prospective study of copy number variations in colon cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of DCC and ERBB2 is the most important prognostic biomarker in Stage II–IIIA colon cancer.
the presence of 2 or more alterations of the 8 selected genes, DCC, EGFR, TP53, BLK, MYC, APC, ERBB2 and STK6, in MSS colon cancer is a significant independent prognostic factor for DFS.
the presence of a DCC deletion and/or an ERBB2 amplification is an independent prognostic factor for relapse in Stage II–IIIC colon cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of DCC and ERBB2 is an independent prognostic factor for Stage II–III patients.
the combination of DCC and ERBB2 CNVs is a strong prognostic factor in Stage II–IIIA MSS colon cancer.
CNVs at DCC/ 18q and ERB2/17q can be used to stratify patients at high risk of relapse in Stage II–II colon cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of DCC and ERBB2 alterations is associated with a worse prognosis in Stage II–II colon cancer.
